items.stem: President William Howard Taft’s Dollar Diplomacy aimed to advance American influence abroad chiefly by which means?
items.stemEs: La Diplomacia del Dólar del presidente William Howard Taft buscaba promover la influencia estadounidense en el exterior principalmente por cuál medio?

choices.text: Sending naval squadrons on goodwill cruises to display American power in foreign harbours
choices.textEs: Enviar escuadras navales en cruceros de buena voluntad para mostrar el poder estadounidense en puertos extranjeros
choices.explanation: This describes Roosevelt's method, and the Great White Fleet's voyage of 1907 to 1909 is its clearest example. Taft kept the Navy Roosevelt built; he did not use it as his opening move.
choices.misconception: hands Roosevelt's naval display to Taft because both presidents were Republicans

choices.text: Encouraging American bankers to lend to foreign governments so that American money replaced European money
choices.textEs: Alentar a los banqueros estadounidenses a prestar a gobiernos extranjeros para que el dinero estadounidense reemplazara al europeo

choices.text: Withholding recognition from any government that had taken power by force rather than by constitutional means
choices.textEs: Negar el reconocimiento a todo gobierno que hubiera tomado el poder por la fuerza y no por medios constitucionales
choices.explanation: This is Wilson's test, applied against Victoriano Huerta in Mexico from 1913. It broke with the older American practice of recognising whoever actually governed.
choices.misconception: assigns Wilson's recognition test to the president who preceded him

choices.text: Negotiating general arbitration treaties that would send disputes to an international tribunal instead of to war
choices.textEs: Negociar tratados generales de arbitraje que enviaran las disputas a un tribunal internacional en lugar de a la guerra
choices.explanation: Taft genuinely pursued this — the arbitration treaties he and Secretary Knox negotiated in 1911 were his own priority, and the Senate amended them to death. It is a real Taft policy and it is not what Dollar Diplomacy named.
choices.misconception: takes one real Taft foreign policy as the definition of a differently named one

items.dokRationale: Recall of what one named policy did. The student retrieves the mechanism attached to a label; no comparison with the other two presidents' motives is required, and that comparison is what a DOK 2 item on this standard demands.
items.explanation: Taft described the policy himself as substituting dollars for bullets. The point was that an American loan buys a lasting claim on a country's customs revenue, which outlasts any single landing of troops — the motive was economic leverage, not conquest.
items.explanationEs: Taft mismo describió la política como sustituir balas por dólares. El punto era que un préstamo estadounidense compra un derecho duradero sobre los ingresos aduaneros de un país, que sobrevive a cualquier desembarco de tropas: el motivo era la ventaja económica, no la conquista.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable

items.stem: President Theodore Roosevelt’s Big Stick, President William Howard Taft’s Dollar Diplomacy and President Woodrow Wilson’s Moral Diplomacy are taught as three different motives. Which statement best describes what the three produced in the Caribbean and Central America?
items.stemEs: La política del Gran Garrote del presidente Theodore Roosevelt, la Diplomacia del Dólar del presidente William Howard Taft y la Diplomacia Moral del presidente Woodrow Wilson se enseñan como tres motivos distintos. ¿Qué afirmación describe mejor lo que las tres produjeron en el Caribe y Centroamérica?

choices.text: Only the first produced armed intervention, because loans and moral tests worked by persuasion rather than by force
choices.textEs: Solo la primera produjo intervención armada, porque los préstamos y las pruebas morales funcionaban por persuasión y no por la fuerza
choices.explanation: True of the Big Stick and false of the other two. Taft's Nicaraguan loans were secured by Marines who landed in 1912 and stayed, and Wilson ordered more interventions in the region than either predecessor.
choices.misconception: reads a policy's name as a description of how it was carried out

choices.text: All three rested on the Roosevelt Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine, which Wilson formally revoked on taking office in 1913
choices.textEs: Las tres se basaban en el Corolario Roosevelt a la Doctrina Monroe, que Wilson revocó formalmente al asumir el cargo en 1913
choices.explanation: The Corollary of 1904 is real and the first half is close to the mark. Wilson did not revoke it: the formal repudiation came with the Clark Memorandum, written in 1928 and published in 1930, and with the Good Neighbor Policy of the 1930s.
choices.misconception: moves a repudiation of the 1920s and 1930s back into 1913

choices.text: Each produced repeated American armed intervention in the region, whatever motive the policy's name announced
choices.textEs: Cada una produjo intervenciones armadas estadounidenses repetidas en la región, cualquiera que fuera el motivo que anunciara el nombre de la política

choices.text: Each was carried out mainly by the Great White Fleet, the sixteen battleships that circled the globe between 1907 and 1909
choices.textEs: Cada una se llevó a cabo principalmente mediante la Gran Flota Blanca, los dieciséis acorazados que circunnavegaron el globo entre 1907 y 1909
choices.explanation: The voyage happened and it was Roosevelt's. It was a demonstration to Japan and to Europe, not the instrument of Caribbean policy, and it was over before Taft or Wilson took office.
choices.misconception: takes the most memorable image of the period as the mechanism of every policy in it

items.dokRationale: The three labels name motives; the item asks what the practice was. The student must set the stated motive beside the record and notice they diverge, which recalling any one label's definition would not reveal.
items.explanation: Different motives converged on the same instrument. Roosevelt took the Dominican customs house in 1905, Taft sent Marines to Nicaragua in 1912, and Wilson occupied Veracruz in 1914, Haiti in 1915 and the Dominican Republic in 1916 — so the president whose policy is named moral intervened the most often of the three.
items.explanationEs: Motivos distintos convergían en el mismo instrumento. Roosevelt tomó la aduana dominicana en 1905, Taft envió infantes de marina a Nicaragua en 1912, y Wilson ocupó Veracruz en 1914, Haití en 1915 y la República Dominicana en 1916: el presidente cuya política se llama moral intervino con más frecuencia que los otros dos.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable

items.stem: A student asks why President Woodrow Wilson’s Moral Diplomacy is called moral when Wilson ordered more armed interventions in Latin America than either president before him. Which answer is best supported?
items.stemEs: Un estudiante pregunta por qué la Diplomacia Moral del presidente Woodrow Wilson se llama moral si Wilson ordenó más intervenciones armadas en América Latina que cualquiera de los presidentes anteriores. ¿Qué respuesta está mejor fundamentada?

choices.text: The word describes the test Wilson applied before acting — constitutional legitimacy — and not the amount of force he used to apply it.
choices.textEs: La palabra describe la prueba que Wilson aplicaba antes de actuar — la legitimidad constitucional — y no la cantidad de fuerza con que la aplicaba.

choices.text: Most of those interventions were commitments begun under Taft's Dollar Diplomacy that Wilson inherited and merely continued
choices.textEs: La mayoría de esas intervenciones eran compromisos iniciados bajo la Diplomacia del Dólar de Taft que Wilson heredó y simplemente continuó
choices.explanation: Nicaragua was Taft's, so some of this is true. Veracruz in 1914, Haiti in 1915, the Dominican Republic in 1916 and the Punitive Expedition into Mexico in 1916 were Wilson's own orders, and they outnumber what he inherited.
choices.misconception: credits a successor's record to the predecessor whose policy he repudiated

choices.text: The Roosevelt Corollary had already placed the region under American police power, so Wilson's landings needed no justification of their own
choices.textEs: El Corolario Roosevelt ya había puesto la región bajo el poder de policía estadounidense, de modo que los desembarcos de Wilson no necesitaban justificación propia
choices.explanation: The Corollary of 1904 did claim that power, and Wilson's administration leaned on it. It explains what made the landings possible, not why the policy that ordered them is called moral.
choices.misconception: answers how an intervention was authorised when asked why a policy carries its name

choices.text: Wilson withdrew the Marines from Nicaragua in 1914, which reduced the American military presence in the region overall
choices.textEs: Wilson retiró a los infantes de marina de Nicaragua en 1914, lo que redujo la presencia militar estadounidense en la región en general
choices.explanation: The withdrawal is real and the year is wrong by a decade: the legation guard stayed through Wilson's two terms and left in 1925, and Marines returned the following year.
choices.misconception: credits Wilson with a withdrawal that happened under a later administration

items.dokRationale: The student must separate a policy's stated test from its record and explain a tension between them. The question cannot be answered by recalling the definition of moral diplomacy, which is the DOK 1 version of the same content.
items.explanation: The adjective describes the test Wilson set, not the restraint he showed. He asked whether a government had come to power constitutionally, and answering no became a reason to act rather than a reason to stand back — which is why a moral standard produced more landings than an openly strategic one.
items.explanationEs: El adjetivo describe la prueba que Wilson impuso, no la moderación que mostró. Preguntaba si un gobierno había llegado al poder constitucionalmente, y responder que no se convirtió en una razón para actuar y no para abstenerse: por eso una norma moral produjo más desembarcos que una abiertamente estratégica.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable
